summary: A Network Host Status report from Ellen Westheimer of BBN covering April 10 to April 21, 1972. The USC IBM 360/44 was connected to the network, and a terminal IMP was installed at Global Weather Central in Omaha on April 18. It updates RFC 330. It was replaced by RFC 342.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 332 reports ARPANET host status for April 10 through April 21, 1972. It includes expected host roles and connection-test results for the period.

subtitle: An April 1972 host report records two new network connections and test results.

tldr.problem: Network operators needed current information about which hosts were available and what roles they served.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 332 gives host status and test tables for April 10 through April 21, noting the USC IBM 360/44 connection and a Terminal IMP installed at Global Weather Central.
tldr.outcome: RFC 332 updates RFC 330 and was later obsoleted by RFC 342, according to the unit metadata.

today: RFC 332 updates RFC 330 and was obsoleted by RFC 342. It records host status for April 10 through April 21, 1972.

sections.title: The Reporting Period
sections.content: RFC 332 reports the status of most network hosts from April 10 to April 21. During that interval, the IBM 360/44 at the University of Southern California was connected to the network, and a Terminal IMP was installed at Global Weather Central in Omaha on April 18.
sections.plainLanguage: The report covers most hosts over an April period. It notes two network changes: a USC computer was connected and a Terminal IMP was installed in Omaha.

sections.title: Host Roles and Exclusions
sections.content: The report separates hosts not expected to operate regularly as servers from hosts intended only as users. It lists Terminal IMPs and the Network Control Center computer among the user-only group; the latter is described as being used solely for gathering network statistics.
sections.plainLanguage: Some listed machines were expected to serve other sites. Others were user-only or were excluded from daily testing.

sections.title: Daily Test Codes
sections.content: The status table uses O for Open, D for Dead or inaccessible, F for Full, H for 1/2 Open, R for Refused, and T for Timed Out. The RFC defines a timeout as failure to complete the Initial Connection Protocol and open a connection within 60 seconds.
sections.plainLanguage: Each test result is a letter describing what happened when the BBN Terminal IMP tried to connect. The table defines the letters and what each result means.
